name: Hershey
description: Hershey makes chocolate and other candy (Hershey's, Reese's, Kisses, Jolly Rancher, Ice Breakers), plus salty snacks (SkinnyPop, Dot's Pretzels, Pirates Booty, LesserEvil). It sells mainly to US convenience stores, grocers, drug stores, clubs and mass merchants, and one wholesale distributor, McLane, took 27% of 2025 net sales. Profit depends on the gap between shelf prices and cocoa, sugar and dairy costs; cocoa is the most significant raw material and Hershey buys it through its own Swiss trading company and hedges with futures. In 2025 cocoa and tariff costs cut the core North America Confectionery segment's income by 15.3% even though a July 2025 price rise lifted sales 4.0%. Salty Snacks is small (11% of sales) but growing faster; International is barely profitable.

gics.note: Conventional filing: sector and sub-industry from Wikipedia's List of S&P 500 companies (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_S%26P_500_companies, read 2026-09-30); industry group and industry are not on that page, so null. EDGAR SIC 2060 (Sugar & Confectionery Products).

hq.note: Wikipedia S&P 500 list and EDGAR business address both give Hershey, PA

employees.note: About 17,550 full-time plus 2,045 part-time (sum computed); about 28% covered by collective bargaining (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: North America Confectionery
businessLines.how: Retailers and distributors buy candy at list price on frequent repeat orders; 2025 growth came from about 6% price with volume down about 2%. Margin is squeezed or widened by cocoa, sugar and dairy costs, which are hedged but not eliminated. Small extras are store sales and trademark licence fees.
businessLines.description: Chocolate and non-chocolate candy, gum and mints, protein bars, spreads, baking and pantry lines, plus Hershey's Chocolate World retail stores (Hershey, New York, Las Vegas, Niagara Falls, Singapore) and licensing of its trademarks to third parties.

operatingProfit.note: Segment income; total segment income $2,738.9M before $807.9M unallocated corporate expense and $423.2M unallocated mark-to-market losses on commodity derivatives. FY2024: $2,945.7M (-15.3%). H1 2026 segment income $1,498.2M vs $1,200.3M in H1 2025.

businessLines.name: North America Salty Snacks
businessLines.how: Retailers buy bags of snacks at list price with recurring orders; growth is driven by volume and new distribution, and Hershey owns popcorn co-manufacturing capacity (Weaver, bought May 2023).
businessLines.description: Ready-to-eat popcorn (SkinnyPop, LesserEvil, acquired 2025-11-18), Pirates Booty baked snacks, Dot's Homestyle Pretzels, other snacks; US only.

businessLines.name: International
businessLines.how: Local distributors and retailers buy Hershey's brands in export and local markets at list price; the segment is small and earned only $3.3M of segment income in 2025.
businessLines.description: Confectionery and snacks sold outside the US and Canada, plus licensed and exported brands.

operatingProfit.note: Down 97.0% from $111.5M in FY2024. H1 2026 segment income $10.1M vs $48.5M in H1 2025.

brands.name: Hershey's, Reese's, Kisses, Jolly Rancher and other chocolate and non-chocolate brands
brands.share: Segment is 81.1% of FY2025 net sales; per-brand sales not disclosed in the sources read

brands.name: SkinnyPop, LesserEvil, Pirates Booty, Dot's Homestyle Pretzels
brands.share: Segment is 10.9% of FY2025 net sales; per-brand sales not disclosed
